fpr.ratio: Net Worth/Total Assets for Prompt Corrective Action
fpr.guide: FPR Ratio and Formula Guide v3.3, June 30, 2023 (https://ncua.gov/files/publications/analysis/fpr-ratio-formula-guide.pdf), pp. 4-5
fpr.result: Matched to two decimals for charters 808, 61559, 66143, 9566 and 62783, 2026-06 (docs/research/fpr-check.md, saved pages in docs/research/fpr-2026-06/).

measures.note: Printed as filed. 998 is NCUA's prompt corrective action ratio: from 2023 it includes the CECL transition provision (NW0004), which the FPR's separate 'excluding CECL Transition Provision' ratio leaves out. For the five hand-check charters, 997 / 010 x 100, rounded to two decimals, equals 998 / 100 in 2026-06. (An early note had 66143 and 9566 off by 0.01 point; that was our rounding, not NCUA's.)

checks.rule: round2(100 * ACCT_997 / D) == ACCT_998 / 100 within 0.01, where D is the first nonzero of ACCT_010A, ACCT_010B, ACCT_010C, less ACCT_LC0047 plus ACCT_NW0004; otherwise ACCT_NW0010; before ACCT_NW0010 exists, ACCT_010
checks.why: The instructions' formula for 998 (p. 127). It reproduces the filed ratio for all 1,359 New Mexico filings, 2018-03 to 2026-06 (113 with an election, 905 on NW0010, 341 on 010). A mismatch is flagged.

measures.label: Net charge-offs, last 12 months
measures.plain_words: Loans written off as lost, less what was later recovered, over the past year.
measures.formula: ((ACCT_550 - ACCT_551)[q] + (ACCT_550 - ACCT_551)[prior December] - (ACCT_550 - ACCT_551)[q minus 4 quarters]) / ((ACCT_025B[q] + ACCT_025B[q minus 4 quarters]) / 2) * 100
measures.scaling: 550 and 551 are year-to-date and reset each January; the formula takes the last 12 months. In a December quarter it is the year's own figure. It needs the December and the quarter a year earlier, so 2018-03 to 2018-09 are null; 2018-12 uses the 2017-12 filing, read for that and not published.

measures.label: Credit card rate
measures.plain_words: What it charges on a credit card.
measures.scaling: Stored as the percent times 100. A 0 comes with no loans of that kind on its books (the instructions ask for loans that have a balance): null, with "No rate reported: none of these loans on its books" in notes, never 0%. Outside 1% to 30%, tested before rounding: null and withheld.

accounts.ncua_name: Interest Rate of Unsecured Credit Card Loans
accounts.ncua_description: Rate of Unsecured Credit Card Loans amount.
accounts.form: Schedule A, Section 1, Item 1, interest rate column
accounts.instructions: Call Report Form 5300 Instructions, effective Sept. 30, 2025 (https://ncua.gov/files/publications/regulations/call-report-instructions-september-2025.pdf), pp. 50, 51
accounts.note: The instructions: "Report loan interest rates being offered as of the reporting period for each loan category. Report the actual rate (report 6.5 for 6.5%). If a loan type only includes purchased loans, report the most common yield on the loans purchased (yield should include the impact of any premiums or discounts). If more than one rate applies, report the most common rate in each loan category." The files store it times 100: 664 is 6.64%.

measures.caveat: The most common rate the credit union offered on the last day of the quarter, as it reported it; for a kind of loan it only buys from other lenders, the most common yield instead. Not a quote, and not the rate a given borrower gets, which depends on credit and term.

fpr.checked_instead: No FPR equivalent. One day's most common offered rate, self-reported. Checked by reading the raw zip for the hand-check credit unions and comparing with each credit union's own posted rates (a later date, so a plausibility check, not a match).

measures.note: 0 for 14 of 37 in 2026-06: most of them don't offer cards.
